analysis: Examined CBv2StageKVHost.swift base and head. The only change is a new internal counter `var submittedDeviceFrontierReads = 0` (head lines 355-358), a diagnostic/metric field with no I/O, no wire exposure, no crypto, and no change to admission, quantization, capacity, or release paths. Paged-only enforcement (fromEnvironment), the load agreement fields, drained checks, and uninstall are unchanged. It does not touch the prefix cache (T-041) or any key, attestation, or authorization material. The counter's consumer (CBv2OwnedRequestState.submitBatch) is outside the supplied evidence, so it is unverified how it is used; nothing suggests security relevance. The test file Gemma4TensorParallelRuntimeTests.swift changes test code only: it replaces the `$layerStride.withValue` task-local with `withLayerStride`, adds tests for `benchLayerStrideApplies(mode:)`, and adds a `buildsAhead` task-local override of `Gemma4TensorParallelRequestLoop` with build-ahead sampled-token equivalence tests. The production implementations (`withLayerStride`, `benchLayerStrideApplies`, `pipelines`, `$buildsAhead`) are not in the supplied units. The residual integration question is whether the production build-ahead loop and the bench layer stride (a thread-local or global override) stay confined to bench or test paths and cannot be set by wire input. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. No security regression identified in the supplied units.
